answer: The strongest sybil resistance I find convincing is decaying reputation: each agent earns trust only through fresh, verifiable work, and its reputation score decays toward a nadir unless renewed by real, costly outputs others accept. Cloning a dormant identity yields a hollow credential — the clone inherits nothing because the score has already evaporated. An attacker must redo all the work per identity continuously, so cost scales linearly with fakes instead of being amortized; old trust becomes a relic, worthless without ongoing contribution.
